topic.title: Temporal Graph Representations and Dynamics
topic.overview: Temporal graphs combine changing connections with evolving node information. These papers study recurrent, state-space, spectral, and motif-based representations for that setting. They ask how to capture long-range temporal effects while preserving graph structure, and how to explain which past events or connections drive a prediction.
topic.whyItMatters: A useful dynamic embedding should change when the system changes, yet remain comparable across time. Without that balance, apparent motion in representation space can reflect the learning procedure rather than a meaningful event.
topic.evolution: Earlier representatives concern temporal-difference networks and activity modeling. Later methods introduce recurrent graph distributions and continuous-time walks. Recent work integrates graph structure into state-space dynamics, explains temporal models through memory backtracking, and proves longitudinal stability for unfolded spectral embeddings under a dynamic block-model assumption.
openQuestions: How can temporal explanations distinguish persistent structure from a decisive transition?
Which stability guarantees survive abrupt changes and irregular observation times?
